To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) reliability economies of scale are important for island power systems, and (2) reliability economies of scales are not large enough to make the size of an island system irrelevant to its reliability.
the reliability of a tropical island system is a function of its size.
the reliability of island systems is positively related to the number of generating plants, the number of transmission lines and the number of substations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reliability economies of scale for electric power systems on tropical islands.
the reliability economics of electric power generation on small islands.
the effect of scale and technological change on the reliability of tropical islands' electric power systems, and with the effect of reliability on the choice of scale and technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the economies of scale for reliability are not great for island power systems.
the scale economies of reliability are significant and that they should be given serious consideration by island power system operators in the planning of their systems.
the reliability of electric power systems in the tropics has not improved over the last 15 years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the economies of scale for reliability in island power systems are small, but the reliability benefits of scale are real, especially in small islands.
reliability economies of scale are important to the operators of tropical island electric power systems.
, in a tropical island environment, there are significant economies of scale in electric power reliability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the economies of scale for reliability in electric power are not as large as the economies of scale in cost.
the scale of an island power system is an important factor in its reliability.
reliability economies of scale are important for small systems and that they can be achieved with relatively small investments in new technology.
